title: Phantom Blade Zero Boss List - Every Boss Confirmed Before Launch
description: Every Phantom Blade Zero boss confirmed before the 29 October 2026 release: 11 named encounters, where each was shown, and the one official rule about what they drop. The director puts the total at 50 or more.

sections.title: The Short Answer
sections.content:
The director stated in October 2026 that Phantom Blade Zero has at least 50 bosses. Before release, 11 of them are named or clearly identifiable from footage S-GAME actually published. That gap is the honest shape of this page: a roster of what exists, not a strategy guide for fights nobody has finished under review conditions.

Two things make a list more useful than a walkthrough here. The first is S-GAME's own design rule: beating a boss gives you its weapon and its signature technique, so the boss list doubles as the weapon list, and the closest thing to a build guide this game has. The second is that the fight itself is the part the reviews agree on - what varies is everything around it, which is what the notes below are for.

sections.title: What Bosses Drop
sections.content:
The rule, from S-GAME's own PlayStation Blog deep dive and repeated in the store copy: defeating powerful foes yields their weapons, and with them the signature techniques those foes used. The director has said the boss count and the weapon count track each other for that reason.

What is not available: a per-boss drop table. No source states that the Puppet Boss gives a specific blade or that a given Phantom Edge comes from a specific fight, so none is printed here. Any site listing exact drops before launch is filling a table from the rule rather than from data. On launch day this section becomes a real mapping - see weapons and Phantom Edges for the rosters the drops feed into.

sections.title: How Many, How Long
sections.content:
• 50 bosses minimum - the director, October 2026 preview coverage.
  • 30-plus main weapons and 20-plus Phantom Edges - official; the same reason the boss list and the weapon list converge.
  • 50 hours (IGN) and 55 hours (Combo Infinito) reported by reviewers on 25-26 October - see how long to beat.
  • The Hunt is the only encounter shown both as an opening pursuit and as a standalone fight, which is why it appears here with its own page.

sections.title: What The Reviews Say About The Boss Fights
sections.content:
Reviews lifted 25-26 October 2026, and bosses sit on both sides of the argument:

  • Praised almost without exception. Saudi Gamer's 100 calls the boss encounters "truly spectacular"; screenactu's 98 says the combat system "should be taught in every game design school"; Areajugones (95) says the bosses "burst with invention"; Game*Spark (9/10) lists the varied boss fights among its highlights.
  • Pacing is the repeated complaint. Eurogamer's 6/10 - the only mixed score in the set - describes the shift from expressive crowd fights to boss fights as losing your power, "like you're waiting your turn to get hits in with a wooden sword".
  • Individual fights can run long. Critical Hits, whose review leaked before the embargo, said some major boss fights felt overly drawn out.
  • The enemies between bosses are the weak link. GameSpot (8/10) says mowing down crowds that barely resist gets tiring and hides how good the boss fights are.

Read together: budget more time than a boss count suggests, and expect the fights to be the part you remember. Full scores here.

sections.title: What This Page Still Cannot Answer
sections.content:
• Which bosses are missable. S-GAME has not said. Community coverage warns some side content cannot be recovered, but no boss is named in that warning - see missable content.
  • Weaknesses and resistances. Nothing published. Every boss page here says "not confirmed" rather than guessing from a boss's appearance.
  • Phase counts. Only two-phase structure is known for a couple of fights from footage; reviewer notes about retrying phase two without replaying phase one suggest the pattern is common, but it is not documented per fight.
  • The full roster. 11 named against a stated 50-plus. The gap is real, and it will close in days rather than weeks.

sections.title: Verification Status
sections.content: Compiled 27 October 2026 from: S-GAME's PlayStation Blog deep dive (11 August 2026) and the launch trailer (21-22 October 2026) for the encounters, the October 2026 preview coverage for the 50-boss figure, and Metacritic-listed reviews for the criticism. Each boss page carries its own source line. This list updates as footage and then player reports confirm the rest; entries are only added here when a specific source names them.
